The Big Story · Climate Science

The clouds carried 10% more water. Japan got 20% more rain.

Scientists reran six record downpours without human-caused warming. Every event weakened—and in one typhoon, the simulated area above 300 millimeters almost halved.

Culture · Books · Opens today

Tokyo turned 500 meters of pavement into a million-book treasure hunt.

The 66th Kanda Used Book Festival opened in Jimbocho with more than 100 wagons. Its real engine is a 160-year-old network of schools, publishers and specialist booksellers.

Science · Hokkaido University

A bird’s wing carries a tiny ecosystem.

Researchers reported today that feather mites form structured communities across a bird’s plumage, offering a model for studying how habitats are divided on a living, moving host.

Ueno Park becomes a city-licensed stage.

Japanese word of the day大雨 · おおあめ · ōame

Heavy rain. 大 means “big” or “great,” and 雨 means “rain.” Unlike a poetic label, ōame is operational language: it appears in weather forecasts, warnings, disaster pages and the formal name 大雨特別警報 (ōame tokubetsu keihō), an emergency warning for extraordinary heavy rain.

Example: 大雨に警戒してください—“Please stay alert for heavy rain.” Today’s attribution study looks backward at six ōame events; during a live event, follow official instructions first. Learn Japanese in context with DraMap for iOS.
